description: Explore three Python patterns that achieve recursion without a standard def statement: default arguments, a callable wrapper class, and a shared dictionary.

steps.description: Look at Pattern 1, which passes a recursive callable through a default parameter rec=None, though line 4 still references factorial_default by name.
Define the Recursive wrapper class, which stores a function self.f and forwards self as the first argument inside __call__.

steps.answer: The Recursive instance factorial_class itself, because __call__ invokes self.f(self, *args).
steps.question: When factorial_class(6) runs, what object is bound to the lambda's first parameter self on line 17?

steps.description: Wrap lambda self, n: 1 if n == 0 else n * self(n-1) in Recursive and call factorial_class(6) to print 720.
In Pattern 3, store two lambdas in a shared dictionary namespace so 'even' and 'odd' can look each other up at call time.
Watch Recursive.__call__ pass self into self.f(self, *args) during factorial_class(6).

title: Practical Fixed-Point Idioms in Python
